item.title: A foreign policy adviser to Netanyahu talks about Israel's stance on war with Iran
item.summary: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with Ophir Falk, foreign policy adviser to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, about his country's stance on war with Iran and Hezbollah.

item.title: Judge rules White House ballroom construction must halt until Congress OK's it
item.summary: Trump responded to the ruling by complaining that the National Trust for Historic Preservation doesn't appreciate his efforts at "sprucing up" Washington's buildings.

item.title: Domino, the warty frogfish, is the first of its kind to be raised in captivity
item.summary: Scientists say the little fish may hold broader lessons for raising other marine species in captivity.

item.title: Trump signs a new executive order on voting. Experts say he lacks the authority
item.summary: Trump's executive order seeks to create lists of U.S. citizens who are eligible to vote in each state, and instruct the U.S. Postal Service to send mail ballots only to verified voters.

item.title: Runners misled at a qualifier race will still get invites to the world championship
item.summary: The U.S. will nearly double its contingent for the women's half marathon championship to fix what officials call an unprecedented problem: an official vehicle took the leading runners off the course.

item.title: Federal judge finds Trump violated free speech by ordering NPR defunded
item.summary: A U.S. District Court judge found that President Trump's executive order calling for the defunding of NPR and PBS violated the First Amendment.

item.title: Trump shares a look at his future presidential library. Here's what to know about it
item.summary: Trump posted the first architectural renderings of his future presidential library, planned for a prime plot of land donated by Miami Dade College.

item.title: The wellness world is eager for RFK Jr.'s promised move on peptides
item.summary: A month ago, Health Secretary Kennedy said his agency would soon give compounding pharmacies the greenlight to make the products, which have exploded in popularity despite a lack of data.

item.title: One of the first people known to change their gender was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh
item.summary: NPR art director and illustrator Jackie Lay tells the story of Hatshepsut, who is widely regarded as one of the greatest pharaohs in Egypt's history — but whose legacy was erased for over 3,000 years.

item.title: Supreme Court opens door to controversial conversion therapy
item.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that Colorado's law banning conversion therapy "regulates speech based on viewpoint."
